summary: 7/7 acceptance criteria covered: 4 new browser checks (all passed) + 6 new backend test files (13 test functions: 11 passed, 2 failed with confirmed reproducible bugs). 2 real bugs found in Open Facts integration (pagination has_more miscalculation + catalog_source cache mislabeling); everything else - category tree, Obst subcategories, Grundsortiment staples, Haushalt/Drogerie catalogs, region-without-market-register fallback, and the full DE/Berlin -> Obst -> Bananen -> watchlist UI flow - works correctly.

bugs.criterion: Verpackte Lebensmittel und Getränke werden weltweit paginiert aus Open Facts geladen.
bugs.description: GET /api/products/search with category=limonaden, country=US, city=Chicago, page_size=24 (the frontend's default page size) returns total=677 but has_more=false, and the UI's 'Weitere Produkte' button is rendered disabled despite '677 Treffer' showing on screen. Root cause in backend/lib/product_catalog.py::search_open_food_products: when Open Food Facts returns a page where one raw item is dropped by map_off_product() (missing product name/code - common upstream data quality issue), the mapped-products count (23) falls one short of page_size (24), so has_more = len(external_products) >= page_size evaluates False even though total is in the hundreds. This incomplete/undercounted page then gets cached for 12h (CACHE_TTL_HOURS), so the bug persists deterministically for that region/category/page_size combo until the cache expires - it is not just occasional flakiness.
bugs.evidence: curl -G 'http://localhost:8001/api/products/search' --data-urlencode 'q=limonaden' --data-urlencode 'category=limonaden' --data-urlencode 'country=US' --data-urlencode 'city=Chicago' --data-urlencode 'page=1' --data-urlencode 'page_size=24' -> {"total":677,"has_more":false,"page_size":24,"results":[...23 items...]}. Cross-checked live in the browser (check 'us-chicago-limonaden-pagination-works'): page shows '677 Treffer' but data-testid=catalog-next-page renders disabled. pytest test_tscheck_openfacts_pagination_worldwide.py::test_us_chicago_limonaden_next_page_is_reachable reproduces this deterministically.

bugs.criterion: Haushalt und Drogerie nutzen die passenden Open-Facts-Kataloge.
bugs.description: backend/lib/product_catalog.py::search_open_food_products sets `source = "Open Food Facts · Cache" if payload else "Open Food Facts"` before checking whether `payload` came from an existing DB cache hit, and never re-derives the label from the cached payload's `catalogs` field on a cache hit. So the first (uncached) call for a Haushalt/Drogerie query correctly reports catalog_source='Open Products Facts' / 'Open Beauty Facts', but every subsequent cached call for the same query mislabels catalog_source as the generic 'Open Food Facts · Cache' even though the served products are still Open Products/Beauty Facts items. Cosmetic/attribution bug, not a data-correctness bug (the actual products/offers returned are correct).
bugs.evidence: curl (cache cleared) -> catalog_source='Open Products Facts'. Immediate repeat curl with identical params -> catalog_source='Open Food Facts · Cache' while returning the same 8 Open Products Facts items. pytest test_tscheck_household_drogerie_catalogs.py::test_cached_waschmittel_catalog_source_label_is_correct reproduces this deterministically.

action_items: Fix has_more computation in search_open_food_products to compare against `total` (or refetch to compensate for OFF items dropped during mapping) instead of the raw per-page mapped-item count, and avoid caching an undercounted page as if it were complete.
Fix the catalog_source label on cache hits to be derived from the cached payload's `catalogs` list rather than the hardcoded 'Open Food Facts · Cache' string.

Updated pre-existing test_tscheck_product_search_no_region_data.py: it previously asserted results==[] for US/Chicago 'piza', which is now stale given this iteration's documented spec_deviation (worldwide Open Facts catalog products stay visible for any region, with offers filtered to that region's approved chains). Rewrote it to assert the new, intended behavior: results are populated from the worldwide catalog and every attached offer still belongs only to US chains.
